brief.headline: Push for ₹28.69 L/year in price cuts to match Mars and Premier while offering 30-day payment for a 4-5% discount — you're 47.43% of their sales, so they can't afford to lose you.

priceAsk.summary: Cut prices on caps and bottles to match Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic, saving us ₹28.69 L/year.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.81/NOS for PP CAP PLAS 28MM (vs our ₹1.08), ₹1.38/NOS for HDPE BOT WHITE 30ML (vs our ₹1.53), and ₹0.35/NOS for MESU. CUP 30MM (vs our ₹0.46).
priceAsk.basis: Mars Plastics charges us ₹0.81 for the 28mm cap — a 33.2% gap — and ₹1.38 for the bottle (10.7% gap); Premier charges ₹0.35 for the measuring cup (30.6% gap). These three SKUs alone cost us ₹28.69 L extra each year. Open-market asking prices for 28mm induction-wad PP caps run ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95), so even at higher volume our ₹1.08 sits at the top; headroom exists down to ₹0.65–0.80.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days to 30 days, and offer 15 days for a 4-5% discount on top.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: 30-day terms free up ₹16.02 L in cash for us; paying in 15 days frees another ₹8.01 L. They borrow money at about 4.54% officially (charged 8%), so paying 30 days early is worth roughly 4-5% to them — ask for that much off the price in return for fast payment.

brief.financialLeverage: They're a small outfit — ₹4.11 Cr in sales, so our ₹1.95 Cr is 47.43% of everything they sell. That's huge leverage: losing us would cut their revenue nearly in half. They keep only 6.0% profit on each sale (similar firms keep 15.0%), so they run tight margins and can't afford big price cuts without volume or payment help. They owe 1.13 times their own cash and their Altman score sits at 1.83 (grey zone — not distressed but not rock-solid either), so cash matters to them. They already take 39 days to pay their own suppliers (vs 23 for peers), meaning they stretch bills to manage cash. Use your size to demand better prices, but offer faster payment as the sweetener — it's worth real money to them and costs us less than the price gap we're paying now.

evidence.point: We pay ₹28.69 L more each year than the cheapest prices we already get from Mars and Premier.
Our ₹1.95 Cr spend is nearly half their total sales.
They keep far less profit per sale than similar firms.
They owe a lot relative to their own cash.
They take longer to pay their own suppliers than peers do.
Their financial health sits in the grey zone — not failing but not strong.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms at scale; top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed moulded and blow-moulded packaging house (₹701.17 Cr revenue, health C 51/100) with broad bottle and cap capability.

risks: They're small (₹4.11 Cr) and in the grey financial zone (1.83 Altman score) — pushing too hard on price alone could tip them over; balance the price ask with faster payment and volume commitment to keep supply steady.

We're 47.43% of their business — if they lose us they may not survive, but that also means they might accept terms that squeeze them too thin and then fail mid-contract; line up Manjushree or Mold-Tek now so we have a fallback.

They keep only 6.0% profit vs 15.0% for peers, so every rupee of price cut hurts them more than a healthier supplier — frame the ask around matching our existing best prices (Mars, Premier) rather than an across-the-board percentage cut.

Their cash is stuck for 101 days (vs 107 for peers) and they owe 1.13x their equity — they value fast payment highly, so use that lever hard but don't let them dodge the price conversation by offering only terms.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're sitting on a ₹28.69 lakh price gap versus Mars and Premier on the same items — let's close that gap today, and in return I can talk about moving you to 30-day or even 15-day payment.
